resumen: Make para crear o producir algo: make a decision, make a mistake, make a noise, make an effort, make progress.
Do para tareas, trabajos y actividades: do homework, do research, do the shopping, do a course, do someone a favour.
Take / have / give / pay / catch / keep: take a break, take a photo · have a good time · give advice · pay attention · catch a cold, catch a bus · keep a secret, keep a promise.
Adjetivo + sustantivo: heavy rain / heavy traffic, strong coffee / a strong accent, high standards / high prices; nunca strong rain ni tall prices.
Adverbio + adjetivo: highly unlikely / highly recommended, deeply concerned / deeply grateful, bitterly disappointed; con verbos de opinión, strongly agree.
Familias de palabras: success (sustantivo), succeed (verbo), successful (adjetivo), successfully (adverbio). Antes de elegir, mira qué función pide el hueco.
Sufijos: sustantivos con -tion, -ment, -ness, -ity (information, announcement, kindness, ability); adjetivos con -able, -ful, -less (predictable, useful, useless).
Prefijos negativos: un- (unpredictable), in- (incorrect), im- ante p/m (impossible), il- ante l (illegal), ir- ante r (irresponsible), dis- (dishonest) y mis- = «mal, por error» (misunderstand).

preguntas.q: I can't go out tonight; I have to ___ my homework for tomorrow.
preguntas.x: Con tareas y trabajos se usa do: do homework, do the housework, do an exercise. Make es el calco de «hacer», pero se usa para crear o producir algo (make a cake, make a plan).

preguntas.q: Please don't ___ so much noise; the baby has just fallen asleep.
preguntas.x: Se dice make (a) noise, igual que make a mistake o make a phone call. Do noise es el error típico al traducir «hacer ruido», porque do va con tareas y actividades.

preguntas.q: We ___ a great time at Laura's birthday party last night.
preguntas.x: «Pasarla bien» es have a good/great time. Passed es un calco del español, y spend va con un período concreto (spend the evening, spend two hours), no con a great time.

preguntas.q: We've been studying for three hours. Let's ___ a short break.
preguntas.x: «Tomar un descanso» es take a break (en británico también have a break). Make a break y do a break no tienen ese sentido, y give no forma esta colocación.

preguntas.q: My aunt is a very ___ businesswoman; her company now has offices in five countries.
preguntas.x: Delante de un sustantivo (businesswoman) se necesita un adjetivo: successful. La familia es success (sustantivo), succeed (verbo), successful (adjetivo) y successfully (adverbio).

preguntas.q: Put your coat on or you'll ___ a cold; it's freezing outside.
preguntas.x: Con enfermedades contagiosas se dice catch a cold (también get a cold). Take y grab son calcos de «coger» o «agarrar un resfriado», y make no tiene ese sentido.

preguntas.q: Please ___ attention to the instructions, because the exam rules have changed.
preguntas.x: «Prestar» o «poner atención» es pay attention (to). Put attention y lend attention traducen «poner» y «prestar» palabra por palabra, y make attention no existe.

preguntas.q: Can you ___ a secret? I'm going to apply for a job in another city.
preguntas.x: «Guardar un secreto» es keep a secret (y keep a promise, «cumplir una promesa»). Save y guard traducen «guardar» palabra por palabra, pero no forman esta colocación.

preguntas.q: Which sentence is correct?
preguntas.a: We need to make a decision before we do any more research.
d: We need to do a decision before we make any more research.
We need to make a decision before we make any more research.
We need to do a decision before we do any more research.
preguntas.x: Se dice make a decision (como make a choice, make progress) y do research (como do a course, do business). Las otras oraciones usan el verbo equivocado en al menos una de las dos colocaciones.

preguntas.q: Which sentence is correct?
preguntas.a: We had heavy rain all weekend, so we stayed in and drank strong coffee.
d: We had strong rain all weekend, so we stayed in and drank heavy coffee.
We had heavy rain all weekend, so we stayed in and drank hard coffee.
We had big rain all weekend, so we stayed in and drank strong coffee.
preguntas.x: La lluvia intensa es heavy rain (como heavy traffic) y el café cargado, strong coffee (como strong tea). Strong rain y big rain son calcos de «lluvia fuerte» o «gran lluvia», y hard coffee no se dice.

preguntas.q: The company has very ___ standards, so only a few applicants get through the first interview.
preguntas.x: Con standards, prices, levels o expectations se usa high: high standards. Tall es solo para la altura física de personas, edificios o árboles, y big o large no se combinan con standards.

preguntas.q: We're still waiting for the official ___ of the exam results.
preguntas.x: Tras the official se necesita un sustantivo, y el de announce se forma con -ment conservando la e: announcement (como agreement, improvement). Announcation aplica mal el sufijo -tion, y announce es el verbo.

preguntas.q: The instructions were completely ___; nobody could work out how to set up the printer.
preguntas.x: -less significa «sin»: useless (inútil), careless, homeless; -ful significa «con»: useful, que contradice el resto de la oración. El contrario de useful es useless, no unuseful ni disuseful.

preguntas.q: In most countries it's ___ to drive without a licence.
preguntas.x: Delante de l, el prefijo negativo in- se convierte en il-: illegal, illogical, illiterate. Inlegal copia el «ilegal» del español con la grafía equivocada, y unlegal o dislegal no existen.

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: “Nobody can predict what the weather will do here.”
preguntas.x: Predict + -able = predictable, y su contrario lleva un-: unpredictable. Inpredictable es un calco de «impredecible», esta palabra no termina en -ible y predictable dice lo contrario.

preguntas.q: It's ___ unlikely that the meeting will finish on time; there are fifteen items on the agenda.
preguntas.x: Highly se combina con adjetivos de probabilidad o valoración: highly unlikely, highly likely, highly recommended. Strongly va con verbos de opinión (strongly agree), deeply con sentimientos y heavily con cantidad o intensidad (heavily criticised).

preguntas.q: Many parents are ___ concerned about how much time their children spend online.
preguntas.x: Con sentimientos intensos se usa deeply: deeply concerned, deeply moved, deeply grateful. Bitterly va con disappointed o cold, widely con known o used, y heavily no se combina con concerned.

preguntas.q: Sorry, I ___ your email; I thought the meeting was on Thursday, not Tuesday.
preguntas.x: El prefijo mis- significa «mal, por error»: misread, misunderstand, mispronounce. Read es irregular (read – read – read), así que misreaded no existe; unread es un adjetivo (unread messages), y dis- no se combina con read.

preguntas.q: Leaving the lab door unlocked overnight was completely ___ of him.
preguntas.x: Delante de r, el prefijo in- se convierte en ir-: irresponsible, irregular, irrelevant (igual que pasa a im- delante de p/m: impossible). Unresponsible es el error más frecuente, pero el negativo de responsible es siempre irresponsible.

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: “Nobody can deny that the plan has advantages.”
preguntas.a: The advantages of the plan are undeniable.
d: The advantages of the plan are indeniable.
The advantages of the plan are undeniably.
The advantages of the plan are deniable.
preguntas.x: Deny + -able = deniable (la y pasa a i), y el negativo lleva un-: undeniable. Indeniable calca «innegable», undeniably es el adverbio (no puede ir tras are) y deniable dice lo contrario.
